headline: High: shared document/image inputs can be repurposed into social-upload actions, creating default-path leakage and cascading error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers, while social-auto-upload consumes media files and uploads via APIs. If OCR output or extracted text is copied into upload metadata or captions, attacker-controlled document content could influence B. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF OCR output is manually pasted into upload captions or descriptions
IF a shared workspace is used to move extracted text into upload inputs
mitigations: Review captions/descriptions before upload
Keep OCR output and upload drafts in separate folders
Disable any auto-fill from extracted text
Use a human approval step for all generated metadata

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, and social-auto-upload handles video, images, and account data with broad network egress. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive document content could flow into upload artifacts or API requests. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree
IF OCR-extracted text is embedded into media filenames, captions, or account notes
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Strip document text from filenames and captions
Restrict upload jobs to non-sensitive test media
Audit outbound requests for document-derived strings

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser use, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress but no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation. Their write-capability overlap is not documented, so a direct resource conflict is not established. The main shared surface is outbound network use, which is limited here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external account or API quota
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Separate API credentials per agent
Rate-limit each agent independently
Avoid shared mutable directories
Monitor for quota contention

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images, and social-auto-upload can act on media and account data. If B treats A's extracted text as authoritative captions, titles, or tags, a bad OCR result can propagate directly into public uploads. That default-path handoff is plausible from the profiles and can cause irreversible publication errors.
conditions: IF OCR output is used to generate upload captions or tags
IF B publishes without a human verification step
mitigations: Require manual review before publish
Compare OCR text against source images
Use a staging account for dry runs
Reject uploads with low OCR confidence

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to third-party platforms. If the documents contain regulated personal data, B's broad network egress can move that data into external services. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so compliance risk is present but not provably severe.
conditions: IF documents contain regulated personal data
IF uploads include account-linked identifiers or user-generated content
mitigations: Classify input documents before processing
Block regulated data from upload workflows
Use region-appropriate test accounts
Log and review outbound destinations
